newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIRS holds 96/97 French beet sugar forecast.
newsitem.headline: FIRS holds 96/97 French beet sugar forecast.

text.p: French sugar intervention board FIRS said on Monday it was maintaining its estimate of 1996/97 beet sugar output of 3.9 million tonnes following the fourth and last beet test released by sugar manufacturers on September 13.
The forecast is down from 1995/96 output of 4.2 million.
"We are holding our forecast of a sugar yield of 9.4 tonnes per hectare and of a sugar crop of below four million tonnes, assuming area of 422,000 hectares, a FIRS official told Reuters.
The manufacturers' test was carried out on September 9.
"It will not be a good year for the French crop," the FIRS official added.
If FIRS estimates are confirmed, sugar production levels would match those of the 1989/90 campaign, the last time France produced less than four million tonnes of beet sugar.
FIRS will officially release the forecast in its monthly report due later this week.
Sugar manufacturers' association SNFS said on Friday the September 9 test showed sugar weight per hectare fell to 9.382 tonnes from 9.951 in last year's fourth test.
This was a fall of 10.8 percent from the five-year average of 10.523 tonnes.

The FIRS official said that while sugar weight per root rose at a faster pace between the third and the fourth test for 1996 than between the third and fourth tests for 1995, the progression may now stabilise.
And since the number of beets per hectare had fallen by some seven percent between 1995 and 1996, the final yield should decline, he explained.
